summary:
SpaceHealth is an astronaut health monitoring prototype that tracks 20 parameters in one place: vital signs, stress and sleep, radiation dose, muscle and bone, kidney labs, and hormones. Instead of relying only on general normal ranges, it learns each astronaut's own baseline from their first 7 days. It then flags changes using five checks: range limits, personal-baseline comparison, 72-hour drift, multi-parameter patterns, and an IsolationForest machine-learning model. Every alert names the parameters that changed and why, so nothing is a black box.
Readings come from sensors, lab entry, or a built-in simulator. A validation API rejects impossible values and stores data in SQLite. Results appear in a 12-section dashboard and an interactive 3D astronaut model with clickable body-system markers.
It is built with Python, FastAPI, Streamlit, scikit-learn, and three.js. All data is simulated. It is an educational prototype
details:
SpaceHealth: personal-baseline health monitoring for astronauts

What it does: SpaceHealth tracks 20 health parameters in one place: vital signs, stress and sleep, radiation dose, muscle and bone, kidney labs and hormones. Instead of only comparing readings to general normal ranges, it learns each astronaut's own baseline from their first 7 days. It then flags deviations using five checks: range limits, personal-baseline z-scores, 72-hour drift, multi-parameter patterns, and an IsolationForest machine-learning model. Every alert lists the parameters that changed and the reason,

Benefits and impact: In long missions, small personal changes can matter before a value leaves the normal range. SpaceHealth shows these early, explains them clearly, and could support crew and ground teams in spotting trends such as bone loss, kidney changes, stress or radiation exposure.

How it works: Data comes from sensors (ESP32), manual lab entry or a built-in simulator. A validation API rejects impossible values and stores readings in SQLite. The analysis engine then updates status, alerts and reports. Results are shown in a 12-section dashboard and an interactive 3D astronaut model, where clickable markers show each body system's current values and trend.
